text: True or False: A counting argument shows that MOST binary strings of a given length are highly compressible — their Kolmogorov complexity is far below their length.
explanation: The incompressibility theorem shows the opposite: at most 2^(n−c) − 1 of the 2^n strings of length n have C(x) < n − c, so almost every string is INCOMPRESSIBLE (C(x) ≈ its length). Randomness is the generic case and structure the exception, so the statement reverses the truth.
